node.date_label: 1970 La Possession de Loudun — selected and presented historical texts · 1975 L’écriture de l’histoire · 1980 L’invention du quotidien, 1
node.description: Michel de Certeau joined historical research on religion and mysticism to questions about how histories are written and how people use cultural forms. La Possession de Loudun presents selected historical texts; L’écriture de l’histoire examines historical practice. In The Practice of Everyday Life, he investigates situated ways of operating within imposed systems. His account of users’ creative activities also questions explanations concerned chiefly with disciplinary power. The English preface distinguishes his volume from Luce Giard and Pierre Mayol’s companion work on dwelling and cooking.

proposed_edges.relationship: Situated ways of operating become objects of historical and cultural inquiry
proposed_edges.evidence_note: English preface ix and General Introduction xi–xii examine relational practices and refuse an atomistic model of the user; this is a bounded methodological contribution.

proposed_edges.relationship: Cultural consumption can transform the uses of imposed representations
proposed_edges.evidence_note: General Introduction xii–xiv distinguishes representations and purchase/attendance statistics from what users make with cultural products. This does not establish that every consumer resists power.

proposed_edges.relationship: Questions an account of discipline centred on the apparatus that produces it
proposed_edges.evidence_note: General Introduction xiv–xv directly discusses Discipline and Punish and asks how users appropriate or evade disciplinary arrangements. This specific criticism preserves the acknowledged analytical debt.
